'''Takakura Shrine''' (たかくらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Haramachi-ku|ja|原町区|qid=Q24892679}}, {{ill|Minamisōma|Q642094|qid=Q642094}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}.
Its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is one of the eight shikinaisha shrines in Namekata District listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* It enshrines {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|Q6080112|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}}.
* According to the Sōma-domain historical work ''Ōsōshi'', it enshrines {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takakuraji|Q11668757|qid=Q11668757|lt=Kumano Takakuraji-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}.
** Another theory says it enshrined Izanami-no-Mikoto, Yomotsuchi-moribito, and {{ill|Kikurihime|Q11619891|qid=Q11619891}}, and was called “Hakusan Sansho Gongen.”
* According to records, the sacred object is “five sun” in length.

=== Origin ===
According to ''Ōsōshi'', it is said to be one of the eight shikinaisha shrines in Namekata District among the 100 shikinaisha shrines in Mutsu Province, though details of its enshrinement history are unknown. In ancient times it is said to have stood in Takakura village west of the current site (present Takakura, Haramachi Ward), with broad shrine grounds and many precinct shrines. A former site remains near Akashiba in Baba, Haramachi Ward, at the boundary of Oshikama, Baba, and Ōkido districts. The shrine grounds are thought to have become desolate from war and conflict; though rebuilt, it did not fully recover and became a small shrine.

In {{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 7), lord {{ill|Sōma Yoshitane (daimyo, born 1548)|Q7559115|qid=Q7559115|lt=Sōma Yoshitane}} was dispossessed by order of {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}}, and those donated lands were lost. The shrine steward at that time was young and could not respond, and the lands remained lost thereafter. Trees in the shrine area were also cut and turned into fields, and by the {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} period those lands had become荒廃.

Before that, a man named Endō Hachirōzaemon lived in the village and set up a small shrine at the north end of the old grounds as a guardian deity. His heir and descendants are said to have lived around present Oshikama. In {{ill|1774|Q7697|qid=Q7697}} (An'ei 3), the shrine was rebuilt, and a ridge tag from that time remains. In {{ill|1799|Q7827|qid=Q7827}} (Kansei 11), a field fire burned the shrine buildings. At that time the domain gave 11 ryō 2 bu obtained by selling several hundred cedar trees from the grounds, and the shrine was restored. In {{ill|Human herpesvirus 6|Q6974|qid=Q6974}} ({{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146}} 12), by order of lord {{ill|Sōma Masutane|Q8514605|qid=Q8514605}}, a survey identified this shrine as “Takakura Shrine,” one of the eight Namekata shikinaisha shrines. In that year, one koku of rice field was lent as shrine land in recognition of its history.
